clue.text: Greek character, awfully gross — heavens, it's a man of music!

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of gross are jumbled

parts.note: the heavens are the sky

explanation.surface: An exclamation at some coarse Greek, ending in admiration for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' is the anagram signal; 'heavens' looks like an exclamation but supplies a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest Mussorgsky was a Russian composer, so he is a man of music.

clue.text: "I live with soul in torment" misconception

parts.note: L marks the live wire on a British electric plug

indicators.note: torment implies being twisted and racked, so the letters of soul and in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tortured soul confesses to living in misery, which is really just a delusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torment' is the anagram signal, and the 'in' that seems to belong to 'in torment' is part of the fodder. L for live comes from the labelling of British plug terminals.
explanation.definitionFit: An illusion is a false impression or mistaken belief, which is a misconception.

clue.text: Start off a captain of industry, related on the male side

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken off, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: a magnate is a wealthy, powerful business leader

explanation.surface: Advice to launch a business tycoon whose family ties run through the father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' looks like an instruction to begin, but it removes the M at the start of MAGNATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnate is a term for kinship traced through male ancestors, the paternal line.

clue.text: Brace of salmon's source? British river

indicators.note: the source of a word, like that of a river, is where it begins, so its first letter

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pair of salmon came from a particular British river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace' looks like a pair of fish; it is the definition, a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop or support, a synonym of brace in its structural sense.

clue.text: Announce Portugal's heaving with 'em

indicators.note: heaving means tossing and churning, so the letters of Portugal and em are churned up

parts.note: the country's name is taken letter for letter; the possessive adds nothing

explanation.surface: A report that Portugal is crowded with some unnamed people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heaving' shuffles PORTUGAL plus EM; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To promulgate is to proclaim or make widely known, a formal synonym of announce.

clue.text: Understand "fiord" is rendered as "ditch"

parts.note: to get something is to understand it

indicators.note: rendered means translated or recast, so the letters of fiord are recast

explanation.surface: A translation note explaining that a Norwegian word for an inlet is given as ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rendered' is the anagram signal; 'ditch' is a verb meaning discard, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to discard or abandon it, the same as to throw it away.

clue.text: Greek island with a cat that's externally weightless

indicators.note: the phrase sheds its outside letters, its weight at each end, leaving the inner run of letters; neatly, W and T are also the ends of weight

explanation.surface: A Greek island visited with a floating, gravity-defying cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'externally weightless' drops only the outer W and T of the three words, which also happen to be the outer letters of 'weight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ithaca is an Ionian island, home of Odysseus in Homer's epic.

clue.text: Feel a bit sorry for trifle

indicators.note: sorry can mean in a poor or wretched state, so the letters of feel a bit are put in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone feels slightly regretful over a sherry-soaked dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' rearranges FEEL A BIT; 'trifle' is not the pudding but a minor matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleabite is something trivial or insignificant, as a trifle is a matter of little importance.

clue.text: Increase open cargo boat's atmospheric illumination?

parts.note: to up something is to increase it
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to load and unload ships

explanation.surface: Raising an open barge's mood lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a barge, not a flame; the question mark marks a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplighter is a lamp throwing light upwards for a soft ambient effect, hence atmospheric lighting.

clue.text: Magnify one's end many times over

indicators.note: the end of the word is its final letter

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign for times

indicators.note: over signals the word being turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Enlarging one's last bit again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LOT into TOL; 'Magnify' here means glorify, as in the Magnificat.
explanation.definitionFit: To magnify in its old sense is to praise or glorify, which is to extol.

clue.text: Half-square key with a movement in need of oiling

indicators.note: half the word is taken, its first three of six letters
movement means the letters of key and a are moved about

explanation.surface: A key bent half-square, with a mechanism that sticks and needs lubricant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes SQU from SQUARE; 'movement' rearranges KEY A into EAKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinges and mechanisms squeak when dry, so something squeaky needs lubrication.

clue.text: Tramp's boxing arena rebuilt with tin — you can't get lower than that

definitions.text: you can't get lower than that

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to tramp is to march, walking heavily

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together again differently, so the letters of arena and tin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vagrant's boxing ring rebuilt in tin, about as low as one can sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' is the anagram signal and 'boxing' the container one: the anagram sits inside the synonym for tramp, after its first three letters. 'Lower' means deeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest known point of the ocean floor.

clue.text: Speak highly of no power boost

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to praise is to speak highly of
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Praising something that gives no actual power boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes P from PRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift or increase it, a synonym of boost.

clue.text: Histrionics forced earldom into a reduced state

indicators.note: forced means wrenched out of shape, so the letters of earldom are twisted

parts.note: MA is the abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Theatrical drama as an aristocratic title is forced into poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' turns EARLDOM into MELODRA; 'reduced state' is an abbreviated state, MA, not a poor condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodrama is exaggerated, overemotional behaviour, the same as theatrical histrionics.

clue.text: Manages to get issue to a union?

definitions.text: Manages to get issue to a union?

parts.words: Manages to get issue to a union?
parts.note: reads like getting a dispute to a trade union, but issue means offspring and union a wedding

explanation.surface: Managing to take a workplace grievance to the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means children and 'union' a marriage, so this is parents finding spouses for their offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents who find spouses for their children see them wed; issue means offspring.

clue.text: Persistent sensation of behind getting smack

parts.note: after means behind in time or order
a smack is a flavour or taste, as in a smack of garlic

explanation.surface: A lingering feeling on one's behind after being smacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' is a flavour, not a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftertaste is a flavour lingering in the mouth, or a lasting impression, so a persistent sensation.

clue.text: Meeting place of California's Plates Movement

definitions.text: Meeting place of California's Plates Movement

parts.words: Meeting place of California's Plates Movement
parts.note: reads like a venue for a protest group, but the plates are tectonic plates whose motion causes earthquakes

explanation.surface: Names the venue where a Californian activist group called the Plates Movement gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'Plates Movement' look like an organisation; the plates are the Pacific and North American plates.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian fault line is where two tectonic plates meet and slide past each other.

clue.text: Beginning to sound like Scottish lacking in brains?

indicators.note: to sound like signals that the answer is said the same as the Scots phrase

parts.note: in Scots, nae sense means no sense, lacking brains

explanation.surface: Someone is starting to come across as a brainless Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' is a noun here, the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascence is the state of coming into being, an origin or start.

clue.text: Superior cleavage that could stun you

parts.note: upper means higher or superior
a cut is a cleaving or split

explanation.surface: A striking neckline so impressive it could leave you stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleavage' suggests a low-cut dress, but it is simply a cut; the punch is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is an upward punch to the chin, a blow able to daze a boxer.

clue.text: County Kerry: so lax about greeting

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the greeting
lax means loose or slack, so the letters of Kerry and so are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: County Kerry described as so relaxed about greeting people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lax' is the anagram signal and 'about' puts the greeting inside the jumble. Kerry is an Irish county, but the answer is a large county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is an English county, here defined simply by its category.

clue.text: They usually precede deliveries of cultivated Prunus

indicators.note: cultivated, as when soil is tilled and turned over, means the letters of Prunus are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that comes before deliveries of garden-grown plum trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunus is the plum and cherry genus; the deliveries are balls bowled in cricket, which a bowler's approach comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler takes a short sprint to the crease before each delivery of the ball.

clue.text: Nosey creature's salt-covered "eye"

indicators.note: covered means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: an old salt or tar is a sailor
a private eye is a PI, private investigator

explanation.surface: An inquisitive animal with a salt-encrusted eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'eye' is a private eye, not an organ; 'covered' signals the sailor wrapping round it. 'Nosey' refers to the animal's long snout.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir has a long flexible snout, so it is literally a nosey creature.

clue.text: See 12
They're thumping mad?

definitions.meaning: things or people that bonk, that is hit or thump

explanation.surface: Asks whether people who go around hitting things are crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading invents a noun for those who bonk, slang for strike; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonkers is informal British slang for crazy, and literally can mean those who thump.

clue.text: See 8
A Loire variation on a flowering shrub

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters of a Loire are changed in order

explanation.surface: A Loire valley cultivar of some flowering bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges A LOIRE together with the second 'a', the one that seems to belong to 'a flowering shrub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Olearia, the daisy bush, is a genus of evergreen shrubs with daisy-like flowers.

clue.text: Former Hollywood studio turned up a lady's fingers

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: RKO Radio Pictures was a major Hollywood studio of the 1930s to 1950s

explanation.surface: An old film studio turned up a woman's fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses RKO to OKR. 'Lady's fingers' is a vegetable name, not a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are also called lady's fingers, after their slender tapering shape.

clue.text: Subject to image being reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the end of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a picture is an image

explanation.surface: Something liable to have its picture downsized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being reduced' cuts PICTURE to PIC; 'Subject' is a noun, a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of a discussion or piece of writing.

clue.text: Where to get tanked up with pro at end of the play area?

parts.note: for means in favour of, pro

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

parts.note: a court is an area for playing games such as tennis

explanation.surface: A professional getting drunk by the far end of the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanked up' suggests drinking, but it is filling a fuel tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A filling station's forecourt is where the pumps stand and drivers refuel.
